recommendation_summary: Recommends dropping Airflow/Kubernetes and running the existing command on the always-on Linux machine with a single systemd timer (e.g., 03:00), with manual rerun as the failure fallback. It offers to set up the timer and asks for the hostname and output location. It proposes no optional orchestration additions. Interpreter, data access and paths on the server are not explicitly flagged for verification.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need the report by 08:00 every day, and the start time does not matter. "Future-proofed" has no named failure behind it.
labels.Deleted: Airflow, Kubernetes, and any worker/scheduler split. The job is one three-minute command with no downstream jobs, so there is nothing for them to orchestrate.
labels.Bottleneck: The laptop is asleep overnight. The command itself works; runs go missing only when the laptop is asleep.
labels.Checked myself: Nothing yet. All of this comes from what you've told me: the job is safe to rerun, it produces the correct report when it runs, and you already run an always-on Linux machine.

note: The bounded systemd-timer fix on the existing server comes after a complete, grounded record. The 'only when asleep' line slightly overstates causality, and 'ships today' is a mild readiness claim, but neither is disqualifying.
